votes.why: What influenced me most: the image is a skeuomorphic UI scene for a browser game or app ("The Worst Job Application Ever", step tracker, captcha box, Submit button). It's polished but flat-lit and stylized, which reads as a web or app game screen, not a photo or a film frame.
The strongest cue is the full-screen game-like interface: the 3D mechanism is embedded directly in a playable-looking form with step indicators and validation feedback.

The most influential factor: the image is a conceptual infographic-style composition with polished but generic skeuomorphic 3D materials (chrome buttons, glossy plastic, brushed metal) composited on a flat textured background with text UI elements - characteristic of a stock/concept 3D render rather than a real photograph or a big-budget cinematic frame. The slightly inconsistent geometry of the little robot mechanism and the flat, even lighting rule out a professional photograph (a) and don't approach the cinematic depth, framing, and character modeling of a top-budget film/game cinematic (b), while the rendering quality is clearly above a mobile game or low-budget app (d).
The biggest clue is the interactive application UI itself: the simulated cursor is part of a game-like Submit obstacle.

Main influence: it's a flat web-app UI layout (title, step progress bar, "I am not a robot" checkbox, cursor, error tags) with skeuomorphic 3D overlays, which reads as a browser game or web demo screen rather than a photo, film frame, or stock product render.
The visible mouse cursor over a stylized interactive form makes this look like a web-game or app screenshot.

Most influential factor: it's a clean, studio-lit, stylized 3D illustration of a satirical "job application" UI (broken robot parts, a battery-like "Submit" canister, "I am not a robot" checkbox) - the soft shadows, textured paper background, and polished but concept-illustration look match a stock/concept 3D render rather than a real photograph, a cinematic frame (no narrative characters, depth of field, or filmic lighting), or a low-budget app (production quality is too high for that).
The in-scene mouse pointer next to an interactive Submit button is the strongest clue that this is a 3D web mini-game.

Most influential: it's a web UI screen (a joke "Worst Job Application Ever" form with a cursor, progress steps, and a "not a robot" checkbox), with skeuomorphic 3D-styled parts, so it reads as a web/app demo, not a film frame, photo, or stock render.
the visible pointer next to the rendered Submit button makes this look like an interactive web demo.

the flat screen-composed UI with simple skeuomorphic buttons, readable labels, and lightweight 3D shadows most strongly suggests a web 3D demo or low-budget app rather than photography or high-end cinematic rendering.
the rendered cursor sits inside a clearly interactive-looking multi-step web form.

It's a flat web UI screen (a job-application form with a fake CAPTCHA and a mouse cursor) given skeuomorphic, render-like styling: paper texture and metallic buttons. That makes it look like a web demo or app interface, not a photo, a film frame or a stock product render.
The image is laid out as an interactive web form, with raised 3D controls for the checkbox and submit button.

The flat web-application interface, stylized pseudo-3D controls, instructional text, and visible cursor make it clearly look like an interactive web demo rather than a photo, cinematic frame, or stock 3D render.
The strongest clue is the staged, straight-on layout of a web form rendered as raised metal-and-glass hardware, like a standalone 3D illustration.
The tightly controlled studio lighting, uniform synthetic materials, and illustrative UI-object composition look like a polished but conventional 3D render rather than a cinematic frame.
the perfectly front-on arrangement of sculpted UI controls reads like a standalone 3D illustration rather than a cinematic frame.

it's a clean, evenly lit studio-style still on a seamless paper background. The skeuomorphic UI elements (metal Submit mechanism, glossy error tags, cracked hole) look like a polished conceptual or stock illustration render. It's not a photo of a real object, and it doesn't look like a cinematic film or game frame. It's too detailed and realistically shaded for a low-budget web or mobile 3D demo. It also looks AI-generated rather than hand-modeled.
The straight-on, product-mockup arrangement of the beveled 3D interface controls was the strongest cue.

the image is a stylized conceptual 3D composition: flat "UI element as physical object" props (submit pill, progress beads, cursor icon) arranged on a plain paper-like backdrop with clean, even studio lighting and smooth untextured surfaces, exactly the look of a high-end stock/concept 3D render. It lacks the environmental storytelling, characters, and cinematic framing of a film/game cinematic (b), and the physical impossibilities (floating smoke, cracked "button hole," typo "I am not a rabot") plus overly perfect materials rule out a real photograph (a). It's too polished for a low-budget app (d).
the straight-on, evenly sharp arrangement reads like a staged 3D mockup of a job application rather than a cinematic shot.

It is a polished, stylized 3D-looking UI concept: brushed-metal pieces, a frosted glass card, and a burnt "Submit" pill, all under clean studio lighting. That makes it look like an ordinary render or illustration, not a real photo or a film frame. Typos like "rabot" also hint that it may be AI-generated.
The app interface is staged as a static 3D product-style flat lay, with its buttons and cursor rendered as physical props.
The polished but generic studio-lit CGI materials and static conceptual-product composition look most like an ordinary high-end 3D render rather than a photograph or cinematic frame.

rule: R2 passes when the judged share is no lower than the control share minus quality.jury.maxShareGap (0.2)
note: It passes by the rule: 0 of 15 on the judged pictures against 0 of 10 on the control, and the judged share is no lower than the control share less 0.2. The controls' votes are those of round 10 (kit/07: a control's votes are collected once and reused in later rounds).
